newsitem.title: USA: Qian gives assurances on Hong Kong, other issues.
newsitem.headline: Qian gives assurances on Hong Kong, other issues.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen gave assurances on Tuesday that Hong Kong would retain a "high degree of autonomy" under Beijing's control and said China would never replace the Soviet Union as a world threat.
In an appearance before a U.S.-China business group, Qian predicted a U.S.-China accord on peaceful nuclear cooperation could be finished in time for a fall summit in Washington.

Qian also promised China would open its markets wider, as the United States has demanded, and he called for negotiators to redouble efforts for an agreement on China's bid to join the World Trade Organisation.

On Hong Kong, the British crown colony that reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1, Qian said, "The Hong Kong SAR (Special Administrative Region) will enjoy a high degree of autonomy." Both the White House and the Republican-led U.S. Congress have voiced concern that Hong Kong's political freedoms be maintained."

Qian, in Washington for high-level talks scheduled to include a meeting with President Bill Clinton on Wednesday, criticised unnamed people in the United States who he said were "spreading the China-threat theory."

"According to their argument, China has replaced the former Soviet Union as the main threat to the United States ... These views could not be more wrong," Qian said. "China does not have a tradition of expansion ... (Its) defence policy is completely defensive in nature ... Even if it becomes stronger in the future, China will not pursue aggression and expansion, still less will it seek hegemony."
